title: Google launches new privacy settings for Gemini: chat history can be retained independently, and whether it is used for AI training is up to the user
excerpt: In Gemini's settings menu, there is a new option that is worth opening. On November 25, Google announced a series of new privacy settings for the Gemini app. Us
content_html:
In Gemini's settings menu, there is a new option that is worth opening. On November 25, Google announced a series of new privacy settings for the Gemini app. Users can now keep their chat history while separately deciding whether to let their chats be used to train generative AI models—the two are no longer tied together, and whether to grant permission is entirely up to the user.

One entry point, two things managed separately

The process is not complicated: in the Gemini app, tap the settings icon, and at the bottom of the page you will find the newly added “Activity” option. Tap it and you will be taken to the “Google My Activity” page, where you can use a drop-down menu to turn the relevant feature on or off. In the past, wanting to keep past conversations often meant agreeing by default to have your data used for model training. Now that hidden rule has been broken: Google has split the old bundled switch into two items. Whether to authorize Google to use chat history to train generative AI models is now an independent choice in the user's hands, and the two are not connected.

Read the exceptions carefully

After you turn the feature off, future chats will no longer be used to train generative AI models, but Google has deliberately left one opening—except for feedback content that users actively submit. In other words, if you give feedback on a response, that conversation may still enter the improvement process. An exemption from training does not mean a full exemption. For people who care about privacy, this update returns the most important choice to users: records can still be saved and used as usual, while whether they are used for training is decided separately. As for details such as whether it is on by default and the rollout schedule, Google has not yet elaborated in the announcement. If you want to confirm your account's current status, just take a look at the “Activity” page.
